thread:
nina: RFC follow-up: v2 chat streams now include per-token metadata JSON alongside text (prob, source, score). Some clients expect a plain text token stream. We need a compatibility path that avoids full payload copy for hot paths. Thoughts?

oscar: If we keep NDJSON like `{"text":"a","meta":{...}}
` it's easy for newer clients. For old clients we could emit `data: <text>` style frames by extracting `text` only. Doing that at gateway means parsing JSON for every token. That's expensive.

lia: Option A: client adapter libs that parse JSON and expose legacy plain tokens. Option B: a tiny binary prefix on the stream that says `mode: legacy` and the runtime emits raw tokens when asked. That would require runtime changes but avoids gateway CPU.

mike: Runtime change seems clean long-term. Short-term we can implement a fast-pass extractor at the edge using a lightweight JSON-on-the-fly scanner (no allocation per token) to pull `text` bytes and forward. Lower memory but still CPU. We should benchmark.

compat-bot: note: canary rollout window scheduled at 1777778900. Metric: `compat.struct.extracts_per_sec`.

oscar: Telemetry: capture per-tenant extra-cpu-ns, p95 extra-latency-ms, and mismatch-rate when extracting vs full JSON. Also record error patterns when metadata fields are missing.

nina: Rollout proposal: 1) 72h shadow-mode to compare outputs, 2) edge extractor canary at 1% tenants, 3) runtime mode flag rollout for cohorts if extractor costs too high. Add per-tenant kill switch.

lia: Docs: we should publish migration notes and a snippet for adapter libs (py/js) showing how to read JSON and emit legacy frames. I'll draft and paste examples in this thread.

mike: I'll run microbenchmarks for runtime emission vs edge extractor and post numbers. If runtime wins, schedule a small runtime change RFC for the next cycle.

nina: Action items: nina - update RFC with timeline and rollback gates; oscar - telemetry and cohorts; lia - adapter snippets; mike - perf numbers. Sync after canary.

nina: tagging as RFC follow-up for structured-token stream compatibility.
